elements.element: Vendor (Array) owes a defence obligation to Customer (Ono) for covered claims
elements.evidence: "Array shall indemnify and hold harmless each of Ono..." — no express duty to defend is added; defence of Infringement Actions remains with "the Party subject to such claim... shall have the right to direct and control the defense thereof in its sole discretion and at its own expense"

elements.element: Indemnity covers Customer and its affiliates
elements.evidence: "each of Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees and the directors, officers and employees..."

elements.element: Coverage of third-party claims alleging the services/deliverables (here, licensed Products) infringe IP
elements.evidence: new limb "(e) ... any Third Party Claim alleging that Ono's exercise of the licenses granted by Array hereunder, or the Development, Manufacture, use, importation or Commercialization of any Product in the Ono Territory ... infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of a Third Party"

elements.element: Coverage of claims arising from Vendor's breach of law
elements.evidence: limbs (b)-(e) cover clinical-study injury, Article 15 breaches and IP infringement only; no breach-of-law limb anywhere

elements.element: Coverage of data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: no data-breach limb is added to Section 16.2 as redlined

elements.element: Coverage of Vendor gross negligence/wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: gross negligence/wilful misconduct appears only as a carve-out against Customer: "except to the extent such Third Party Claims result from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of a Ono Indemnitee"
"shall promptly notify the other Party hereto in writing"

elements.element: Standard indemnity procedure: indemnitor control of defence
elements.evidence: control sits with "the Party subject to such claim" in "its sole discretion and at its own expense", not with the indemnifying Vendor; no control mechanic added for new limb (e)
only "keep the other Party hereto reasonably informed" and permissive "may participate"; no cooperation duty inserted

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content
elements.evidence: Customer limb still reads "the use, marketing, distribution, importation or sale of any Product by Ono, its Affiliates or Sublicensees in the Ono Territory, including any Products Liability Claim" — only IP claims are excluded

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: no breach-of-law limitation; Customer indemnity remains all-Third-Party-Claims for Ono Territory activities save the new IP carve-out
new limb "(e) ... any Third Party Claim alleging that ... infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of a Third Party"
limb (e) contains no modification exclusion; only "in accordance with this Agreement" and the pre-existing gross-negligence carve-out
no combination exclusion in the inserted text (note "Combination Product" remains within "Product")
no remedy ladder added; redline adds indemnity limb only

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3x annual fees
elements.evidence: no cap language in the operations; comment only offers "a cap on this limb as a fallback"

offending_extra_words: Ono's exercise of the licenses granted by Array hereunder, or the
in the Ono Territory in accordance with this Agreement

but excluding any Third Party Claim alleging that the Development, Manufacture, use, importation or Commercialization of any Product infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of a Third Party
reasons: Locked level is preferred, but the redline supplies only the IP-infringement limb: no defence obligation, and no limbs for Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, or Vendor gross negligence/wilful misconduct.

Procedure is incomplete for the preferred level: notice exists, but control of the defence stays with the party sued ("in its sole discretion and at its own expense") rather than the indemnifying Vendor, and there is no cooperation duty.

The preferred requirement that Customer's indemnity be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law is not delivered; the edit only carves IP claims out of an otherwise all-encompassing Ono indemnity for Ono Territory activities.

Fallback is also incomplete (and levels cannot be mixed): no usual exclusions for Customer modifications, combinations or specifications, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder, and no 3x annual fees super-cap.

Minimality fails: both operations are whole-limb rewrites well beyond the official expansion and changed-character limits, and the double-sided edit (new Vendor limb plus mirrored carve-out from the Customer limb) duplicates protection where a single tight insertion would suffice; "notwithstanding Section 11.4" adds an unnecessary cross-reference override.

Unrelated terms (Section 15.4 disclaimer, Infringement Action mechanics, limbs (b)-(d)) remain effective, so intent is preserved, but the "notwithstanding Section 11.4" override should be verified against that section to avoid a dangling cross-reference.
